newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia non-CIS Q1 oil exports to rise 19 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Russia non-CIS Q1 oil exports to rise 19 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Russia's Fuel and Energy Ministry has raised Russia's first quarter crude oil export volumes to 28.1 million tonnes from 25.7 million tonnes, ministry spokesman Sergei Nogotkov said.
He said the figure was for exports outside the Commonwealth of Independent States, or CIS, and that it represented an 18.6 percent increase compared to year-ago levels.

Nogotkov also said the ministry had reduced first quarter crude oil exports for state needs to 8.1 million tonnes from 9.2 million tonnes, and that 4.6 million tonnes of that total, or 57 percent, had already been exported.
"This means producers will have more oil to export themselves in the first quarter," he said.
Russian crude oil exports outside the CIS, including transit oil, over the first two months of this year were 17.2 million tonnes, he said.
The figure represented 61 percent of the quarterly scheduled volume. CIS crude oil exports over January-February were 3.2 million tonnes, he said.

Nogotkov said that Surgutneftegaz, Russia's third-largest oil producer, which is allowed to export more to raise cash to build an oil export outlet near St Petersburg on the Finnish Gulf, had already exported 893,000 tonnes over the first two months of this year, a 24 percent rise year-on-year.
LUKoil, Russia's largest oil producer, had exported 69 percent of its first quarter allotment over January-February, he said, without providing an absolute figure.
